topic: Substance misuse screening in mental health patients

audits.title: The hidden cost of not having a dual diagnosis team (an audit looking at inpatient admissions for Redbridge Community Recovery Team West)
audits.standard: NICE CG120 on co-existing severe mental illness and substance misuse
audits.setting: Redbridge Community Recovery Team West, NELFT (inpatient admissions)

cycle1.result: Only 50% of patients with known dual diagnosis had a urine drug screen on admission and 25% of those currently misusing substances were referred to specialist services.

audits.other_findings: Dual diagnosis patients were more often detained (89% v 72%), of no fixed abode (28% v 13%) and non-compliant before admission (83% v 56%).
audits.citation: Bandukda M, Bhenick M, Chaudry N, Getachew H. The hidden cost of not having a dual diagnosis team (an audit looking at inpatient admissions for Redbridge Community Recovery Team West). BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S65-S66.

audits.title: You have to acknowledge the problem before you can address the problem: Audit looking at identification of co-existing substance misuse in a Liaison Psychiatry patient population
audits.standard: NICE: all patients asked about substance use
audits.setting: Ealing Liaison Psychiatry Service, West London NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 69% asked about substance use; none aged over 80, 55% of females and 33.3% of ward referrals asked.

audits.intervention: Training session highlighting results and NICE recommendations.

cycle2.result: 93% asked about substance use; 60% of over-80s, 96% of females and 85% of ward referrals.

audits.citation: McLean E, Kadiwar A, Alexander M. You have to acknowledge the problem before you can address the problem: Audit looking at identification of co-existing substance misuse in a Liaison Psychiatry patient population. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S91-S91.

audits.title: Audit & Reaudit of Assessments Regarding Substance Misuse in Patients Referred to Liaison Psychiatry Service
audits.standard: Assessment of alcohol and drug use and offer of advice, intervention or referral
audits.setting: Liaison psychiatry service, Derriford Hospital (Livewell Southwest)

cycle1.result: Nearly half of patients assessed were not asked about alcohol or drug use.

cycle2.result: Alcohol use asked in 78%, drug use in 77%; 73% of those with an identified problem (n = 15) offered advice or intervention.

audits.other_findings: Documentation of advice or intervention rose by 21% since August 2020. Misuse identified in 10% of those asked about alcohol and 13% of those asked about drugs.
audits.citation: Shittu O, Mushtaq S, Maria D. Audit & Reaudit of Assessments Regarding Substance Misuse in Patients Referred to Liaison Psychiatry Service. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S175-S175.

audits.title: Substance Misuse History Documentation at Admission to Secure Rehabilitation Ward Audit
audits.standard: Electronic admission documentation of substance use history

cycle1.result: 7/12 patients asked about substance misuse at admission review; 5 not asked.

audits.other_findings: 11/12 met ICD-10 harmful use of illegal substances and 9 harmful use of alcohol; reasons and attitudes for use were rarely explored.
audits.citation: Westhead E, Sud N. Substance Misuse History Documentation at Admission to Secure Rehabilitation Ward Audit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S171-S172. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.439.

audits.title: Audit on Drug Screening Practice on Inpatient Psychiatric Wards
audits.standard: Trust policy for drug screening on admission

cycle1.result: Documentation about drug screening in 23/40 (57.5%); test offered to 21/40 (52.5%); 15/21 (71.4%) completed; 5/8 positive results referred to substance misuse services.

audits.other_findings: Reasons for refusal (6, 28.6%) were not documented; re-audit planned after 3 months.
audits.citation: Hamid M, Ahmed M, Shekar M. Audit on Drug Screening Practice on Inpatient Psychiatric Wards. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S240-S240. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10598.

audits.title: Assessment and Management of Substance Misuse Among Patients With Psychosis at a Mental Health Inpatient Unit in CNTW NHS Foundation Trust: An Audit
audits.standard: NICE CG120 Coexisting severe mental illness (psychosis) and substance misuse
audits.setting: Male inpatient wards, St George's Park Hospital, CNTW NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 88.8% assessed for substance use in first week; 62.06% had specialist drug and alcohol service involvement on admission; 87.5% had ward policies followed; 42.8% had specialist involvement on discharge.

audits.intervention: Planned: service evaluation of barriers to specialist service involvement and an educational programme for staff, especially nurses; re-audit in 6 months.
audits.other_findings: Involvement of specialist substance misuse services at admission and discharge remained the weakest area.
audits.citation: Devasia M, Martin G, Thakrar P, Shahzaib R, Erinfolami A. Assessment and Management of Substance Misuse Among Patients With Psychosis at a Mental Health Inpatient Unit in CNTW NHS Foundation Trust: An Audit. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S269-S269. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10657.

audits.title: Use of a quality improvement strategy to increase drug and alcohol consultation and care opportunities for mental health inpatients in rural and remote New South Wales.
audits.setting: Dubbo Hospital inpatient mental health units, rural New South Wales

cycle1.result: Drug and alcohol consultation in 48 of 228 (21%) patients.

audits.intervention: Staff education and discussion, plus a standing morning meeting agenda item to identify and refer patients
audits.citation: Kealy-Bateman W, Christian N, Wetton R, Bruce BJ, Rowe D, McIntyre S.
